contracts: pub enum Until { Plane(Plane) } — module-local target enum, one variant (D2)

pub fn extrude_until(profile: &[Curve], arrangement: &Arrangement, dir: Vector3, target: &Until) -> Outcome<Solid> — certified sweep-to-plane: Empty for a non-terminating sweep (n·dir == 0, non-finite/z-neutral dir, every boundary t < 0) or a straddling plane (partial termination, booked follow-up); UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier) for a non-convex region boundary or a circle edge under an oblique target; parallel target rides the landed extrude_profile_vector at the uniform t*·dir (metamorphic identity); oblique target assembles bottom cap + contact()-certified curtain walls + cap polygon in the target plane through Solid::try_new

pub fn project_profile(profile: &[Curve], arrangement: &Arrangement, dir: Vector3, target: &Until) -> Outcome<Vec<Curve>> — the region boundary's termination loci as curves: parallel target translates each boundary curve by t*·dir (translation preserves the Curve type); oblique target maps each Line edge to the Line between its endpoints' images and refuses a Circle edge UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier); returned carriers are Line/Circle by construction

Termination lines are the landed truck-evidence contact() exact plane_plane arm (certified records, never raw intersections); every witness t is machine-checked against the closed form t(p) = (n·o − n·p)/(n·dir) (BG-NUM-002); the cap face's Plane data equals the target's exactly (same Plane value, compared by data)
deviations: Oblique-target fixture sign (tests 2/3/9): the packet's 'target plane through (0,0,2) with norm (1,0,1)/√2' taken literally is x + z = 2, which STRADDLES the [1,3]² square — t(3,1,0) = −1/2 — and yields a trimmed-bottom wedge, contradicting the packet's own test-2 face count '5 (bottom, 4 walls) plus the oblique cap = 6 total' and test-3's D4 cap-polygon machine-check. The plane is realized as z = x + 2 (through (0,0,2), normal (−1,0,1)/√2), built from the three dyadic points (0,0,2), (1,0,3), (0,1,2): t(x,y) = (2+x)/2 ≥ 1.5 > 0 on [1,3]², cap vertices (1,1,3),(3,1,5),(3,3,5),(1,3,3) exactly the D4 closed-form images, cap box [1,3]×[1,3]×[3,5]. The packet's norm text is sign-sloppy; the operative instruction 'build from three exact dyadic points; compare planes by data' fixes the sign by construction.

Cap vertices are computed by the closed-form projection v' = v + t(v)·dir (dyadic-exact for the witnesses) rather than a 3-D line-line intersection of the termination lines; geometrically v' IS the pairwise intersection of consecutive termination lines, and each vertex is machine-checked to lie on BOTH adjacent contact-certified lines (point-to-line distance ≤ named slack) and in Π (plane residual ≤ named slack) — the packet's machine-check is satisfied with certified records, not raw intersections.

Straddling-plane guard: D3 refuses Empty only when EVERY boundary t < 0 ('some t ≥ 0 → proceed'), but D4's construction (bottom cap = the full region face) is sound only when every boundary t ≥ 0. When the plane cuts through the region the halfspace cut trims the bottom — a trimmed-cap construction outside v1 (booked follow-up) — so the oblique branch machine-checks all boundary t ≥ 0 and refuses Empty otherwise. Defensive; no booked test exercises it (all fixtures have uniform-sign t).

Parallel-target uniformity: D4 asserts t* is uniform for n ∥ dir, which holds when n·p is constant over the z = 0 region (n ∥ ẑ, the fixture class). A parallel target with an oblique dir makes t vary over the region; the parallel branch machine-checks exact uniformity across all boundary vertices and refuses Empty otherwise (unbooked, untested).

project_profile is permissive on the plane-behind case: D3's 'every t < 0 → Empty' is an extrude_until termination rule; the projection onto Π is well-defined for any sign of t, and the packet does not mandate the behind-refusal for project, so project_profile projects regardless (the fixture t values are all positive).
